sections.overview: The sonaghen is a distinctive trout of Lough Melvin in north-west Ireland.
sections.identification: Its historical name, black-finned trout, refers to a notable dark-fin character; it is one of the lake’s three recognized trout forms.
sections.habitat: It is associated with Lough Melvin and its tributary catchment.
sections.diet: The sources consulted here focus on identification and population structure rather than a detailed species-specific diet.
sections.behavior: A recent genetic assessment found the sonaghen population structured across multiple inflowing tributaries.
sections.reproduction: The 2025 assessment reports that sonaghens spawn in multiple tributaries of the lake.
sections.ecology: It coexists in Lough Melvin with gillaroo and ferox trout, treated in a recent study as reproductively isolated forms/species.
sections.conservation: Its lake populations are the subject of genetic monitoring and conservation planning.
